meta_description: OpenDrone is a community project, Incutec is a Belgian startup that started the initiative and hosts this website, sells the products here, and does what the community can't do on their own. Why everything is Open Source, and how the bills get paid.
title: Who designs OpenDrone, and who sells it
lead: Every OpenDrone board comes with its full source on GitHub, and the frames are published there too. The motors are the exception: OEM motors we sell, not open hardware. Incutec is the Belgian startup that started the initiative, hosts this website, sells the products here, and does what the community can't do on their own.
s1_body: The direction of OpenDrone belongs to the people who fly. The community designs, reviews, tests and decides. We try to support where we can.
As contributors arrive, we want to move from designer to maintainer. Plenty of people can design this hardware, and we will help them do it. If you want to help, [here is how](/contributing).
s2_body: Incutec handles the part you cannot fork: production, quality control, distribution, and the legal responsibility for what is sold. That does not change because the design is open. The best support comes from community members helping each other; our job as a small team is to learn to make, test and ship these boards well.

The community project needs no revenue; the company that makes and supports the boards does. We make no money from ads, affiliate trackers, resold analytics, bundled apps or firmware keys. Our analytics are cookieless (Plausible), and the boards work whether or not this shop exists.
s3_title: Why a company is in the loop
s3_body: Incutec is a young startup from Leuven, Belgium, founded in June 2026. We're trying out a new business model where development is decentralised like Open Source code projects, but a company still holds the responsibility of bringing the product to market.

OpenDrone is our pilot project, and FPV is a good place to start: the firmware is already developed in the open, but most of the hardware comes from a few Chinese companies. That is not bad in itself, but they should not be the only ones making it.
s4_body: For the future business model of Incutec, think of it as a music record label for hardware: someone brings us a working design with real demand, and we handle certification, manufacturing, sales and support.

OpenDrone is where we build that pipeline: PCB manufacturing, machining, injection moulding, testing and shipping. Each later project keeps its own team and final assembly, and reuses the route from prototype to sold product.
s5_body: A [packaged product](/collections/all), tested and inspected before it ships, sold by Incutec. The price covers the PCB, components, assembly, testing, packaging, VAT, support and the engineering for the next revision. Shipping is a flat rate per destination ([Shipping](/en/shipping)). Where it is made: [Production](/production).
s6_body: CERN-OHL-S v2 is a reciprocal, copyleft open-hardware licence. It keeps the design open: modify an OpenDrone board, ship your own version, and if someone asks for your sources, you hand them over on the same terms. The point isn't to stop clones. We can't, and we wouldn't want to. The point is that every clone carries its sources forward to the next person.

Eight boards are certified by the Open Source Hardware Association: BE000026 through BE000033, both flight controllers, both ESCs and all four receivers. Each board's product page links its own certificate, repository and issues.
s7_list: If Incutec disappears tomorrow, you still have the files, and the community still owns the project. Anyone, including you, can order a revision and keep it alive.
Want a 4" version, a 3S-only build, a heavier-copper variant? Fork it, change it, fab it. If it's good, open a PR upstream.
Teacher or club? We would rather you copy the design than buy a cheap closed alternative.
s8_body: The store you are reading is also a repository: [OpenDrone-hw/OpenDrone-Web](https://github.com/OpenDrone-hw/OpenDrone-Web). The pages, the 3D hero, the checkout wiring, the tooling that renders the board art: all of it is public.
